item.title: Voice of Revival Radio and Television launched in Port Moresby
item.description: A long-awaited dream is now a reality for the Revival Centers of Papua New Guinea with the official launch of its Voice of Revival digital radio and television station in Port Moresby on Tuesday. The launch coincided with the church’s 44th Anniversary celebrations and was held under the theme “His Voice, Our Voice, Their Voice, the Voice of Revival.”
item.content:encoded:
A long-awaited dream is now a reality for the Revival Centers of Papua New Guinea with the official launch of its Voice of Revival digital radio and television station in Port Moresby on Tuesday.

The launch coincided with the church’s 44th Anniversary celebrations and was held under the theme “His Voice, Our Voice, Their Voice, the Voice of Revival.”

What is now a modern broadcast center was once the church Principal Pastor’s unused office.

The idea to revive a radio station, first announced in 1997, was brought back to life in 2022.

An initial cost of K500,000 was estimated. After prayer and planning, the church began working with the National Information and Communication Technology Authority, NICTA.

Construction started in 2024 and faced challenges with funding, skills and infrastructure.

But with support from the church, congregations, and technical teams from Australia, the facility was completed. It now operates as both a podcast and broadcast center, able to go live on radio and camera.

The station was officially launched on Tuesday, September 1st, 2026 by Founder and Principal Pastor Godfrey Wippon.

NICTA CEO Lume Polume commended the church for using technology to expand the gospel, saying it aligns with government policy.

He urged the church to use the service responsibly and not discriminate against others.

Chief Censor Jim Abani also said content aired on the station must be decent for public consumption.

A radio station certificate was presented during the launch, officially recognizing Voice of Revival as a broadcaster.

Meanwhile, Deputy Managing Director for NBC Michael Samuga pledged NBC’s support towards the newly established Voice of Revival Radio and Digital Television Station.

The platform will now be used to spread the Gospel and the truth, and to reach communities across PNG and beyond.

item.title: Police launch probe into early morning gold robbery
item.description: A major police investigation is underway following an early morning heist in Port Moresby where 10 armed men ambushed a private security convoy and escaped with gold bullion, cash, and firearms. item.content:encoded:
A major police investigation is underway following an early morning heist in Port Moresby where 10 armed men ambushed a private security convoy and escaped with gold bullion, cash, and firearms.

Police Commissioner David Manning confirmed that the armed robbery occurred around 4:30am on Wednesday when two private security vehicles carrying the commercial shipment were intercepted by unknown vehicles.

The heavily armed assailants held the private security personnel at gunpoint before seizing the consignment of gold bullion, cash, and firearms.

Deputy Commissioner of Specialist Operations Donald Yamasombi has been appointed to direct the probe. Investigators are currently interviewing eyewitnesses, security crew members, and management from the security firm.

Manning expressed serious concerns regarding the operation of the private security firm, revealing that police were not informed prior to the high-value transport.

“The gold and cash were being carried by a private security firm and police had not been alerted to the movement prior to it taking place,” Manning said.

“Police are not privy to the standard operating procedures of private security businesses that are contracted to carry commercial valuables.

“This is a very serious incident. Early indications are that the movement of these valuables by the security company leave a lot to be desired in terms of how the private operation was conducted.”

Manning said both the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] and private clients expect the highest level of professional conduct from security management and staff.

He assured that the priority for RPNGC investigators remains the prompt identification of the suspects, the recovery of the stolen property, and a full review of the security firm’s standard procedures.

item.title: Public broadcasters to do more
item.description: The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) Managing Director Hugh Marks said that while the national broadcaster can now reach more Australians than ever before, it is being asked to "do more without more" across an expanding range of platforms. Delivering the keynote address at the ABU Global news forum in Sydney this morning, Mr. Marks said news remains critically important and that he approa
item.content:encoded:
The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) Managing Director Hugh Marks said that while the national broadcaster can now reach more Australians than ever before, it is being asked to "do more without more" across an expanding range of platforms.

Delivering the keynote address at the ABU Global news forum in Sydney this morning, Mr. Marks said news remains critically important and that he approaches the industry’s challenges with optimism.

"We are funded to do broadcast radio, TV, digital and podcast," Marks said. "But we keep adding content platforms without additional resources."

He pointed to recent mistakes, including issues at Four Corners, as examples of what happens due to funding limitations.

"Limitation on funding means we are constantly asked to do more without more."

Mr. Marks said the ABC now faces a "huge audience challenge" because its viewers and listeners are no longer the same.

"With multiple platforms and complex audiences, this is a challenge. But the opportunity is that we can reach more people now than we could before."

The ABC Managing Director said the broadcaster’s role is to balance depth and accessibility while protecting public trust in journalism at a time of rapid change.

Meanwhile, the ABC has welcomed international broadcasters to Sydney for a major forum focused on the future of public media, with ABC Head of International Claire Gorman saying it is an “honor” for the ABC to host.

Speaking at the opening this morning, Gorman said the ABC has a great tradition of hosting important industry events. This year’s gathering has drawn participants from as far as Colombia and Uzbekistan.

The forum is being held under the theme “Resilient Journalism, Safeguarding Truth and Wellbeing”.

"Across the globe information travels fast and AI and disinformation are putting pressure on newsrooms," Gorman said. "Our ABU engagement allows us to adapt to the changing media landscape."

"Our ABU activities mean we are engaging robustly and learning from each other," she said. "Our team and I love to work with our partners across the region."

Gorman also reaffirmed the ABC’s commitment to diversity and inclusion in journalism, saying it must remain central to how public broadcasters serve their audiences.

The ABU brings together public broadcasters from across Asia and the Pacific to share news, resources, and strategies to strengthen trusted media in an era of rapid technological change.

item.title: Media urged to be steadfast
item.description: Traditional media is undergoing rapid change, but public broadcasters must remain steadfast in delivering credible news, especially during times of conflict, disaster, and uncertainty. The Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union Secretary-General Ahmed Nadeem issued this challenge this morning at the opening of the ABU Global News Forum at the ABC office in Sydney, Australia.
item.content:encoded:
Traditional media is undergoing rapid change, but public broadcasters must remain steadfast in delivering credible news, especially during times of conflict, disaster, and uncertainty.

The Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union Secretary-General Ahmed Nadeem issued this challenge this morning at the opening of the ABU Global News Forum at the ABC office in Sydney, Australia.

The forum is themed "Resilient Journalism, Safeguarding Truth and Wellbeing".

Media in PNG and the Asia-Pacific region are experiencing varying challenges, including funding, but have been urged to have a duty of care and remain at the forefront of trusted journalism.

"Trust is important, especially during conflicts, disasters and times of uncertainties," Mr. Nadeem said.

He stressed that one of the most critical areas for public broadcasters is regional reporting, by telling local stories in local voices.

"The important area we serve is accurate news. An area difficult to do, but one we cannot afford to get wrong."

Mr. Nadeem says the ABU, which helps its member countries on capacity building, including the National Broadcasting Corporation, says maintaining public trust must remain the top priority.

It’s being attended by CEOs and news leaders from the 280 ABU member countries.

item.title: Journalists strengthen skills in ethical election reporting and investigative journalism
item.description: Journalists from various media organisations across Papua New Guinea are enhancing their knowledge and skills in ethical election reporting and investigative journalism through a week-long workshop in Port Moresby. The training, funded by the European Union through the United Nations Development Programme [UNDP], began on Monday and will conclude on Friday. It brings together reporters, editors an
item.content:encoded:
Journalists from various media organisations across Papua New Guinea are enhancing their knowledge and skills in ethical election reporting and investigative journalism through a week-long workshop in Port Moresby.

The training, funded by the European Union through the United Nations Development Programme [UNDP], began on Monday and will conclude on Friday. It brings together reporters, editors and media practitioners to improve the quality, accuracy and fairness of election-related reporting ahead of future electoral processes.

The workshop focuses on key areas including ethical journalism, investigative reporting techniques, voter education, combating misinformation and ensuring balanced coverage of candidates and political issues.

Facilitators stressed that a free, fair and credible election depends on an informed public, and that the media has a critical responsibility in providing citizens with accurate and impartial information.

Participants are being equipped with investigative tools to report on issues such as electoral integrity, transparency, intimidation, vote-buying and misinformation, while maintaining professional standards of fairness and independence.

UNDP representatives highlighted that access to reliable information is a fundamental right of every citizen and plays a vital role in strengthening democracy. By empowering journalists with investigative and ethical reporting skills, the programme aims to promote transparency, accountability and public trust in the electoral process.

Media practitioners attending the workshop said the training would enhance their ability to produce fact-based stories that inform voters, amplify community voices and contribute to free, fair and inclusive elections in Papua New Guinea.

item.title: PM in Palau for Pacific leaders meeting
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape is in Palau to join Pacific leaders for a high-level meeting expected to shape discussions on the region’s peace, unity and economic future. The Prime Minister’s arrival also comes just a day after the PNG Government delivered a K1.3 billion supplementary budget in Parliament.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape is in Palau to join Pacific leaders for a high-level meeting expected to shape discussions on the region’s peace, unity and economic future.

The Prime Minister’s arrival also comes just a day after the PNG Government delivered a K1.3 billion supplementary budget in Parliament.

Touching down in Koror, Palau, the PM steps away from domestic politics to focus on regional issues.

This is not Prime Minister Marape’s first Pacific Islands Forum leaders’ meeting.

Over the years, he has used this platform to strengthen regional relationships with neighbouring Pacific nations and advocate for PNG’s interests.

For the Prime Minister , the Pacific Islands Forum remains the premier political gathering of the Pacific.

Marape says PNG will use this latest gathering to reaffirm its commitment to Pacific unity and push for practical initiatives that can strengthen the region’s economic resilience and support long-term prosperity.

Mr Marape and delegation expected to return home on Friday.

item.title: Bulolo starts work on K5.4 million administration building
item.description: Bulolo District has started work on a new K5.4 million administration building in Bulolo Town. The two-storey duplex building is expected to be completed within seven months.
item.content:encoded:
Bulolo District has started work on a new K5.4 million administration building in Bulolo Town.

The two-storey duplex building is expected to be completed within seven months.

Bulolo MP and District Development Authority chairman Sam Basil Jnr says the project will reaffirm Bulolo Town as the district headquarters.

The new building will also provide space for the Bulolo Urban Chamber and other administrative functions.

Bulolo district chief executive officer Joe O’Brien Paru said the project builds on the work of former Bulolo leaders who established the existing administration office.

During construction, the district administration will operate temporarily from Golpu Haus at Zenag in Mumeng LLG.

Basil also announced plans for another project, with a groundbreaking ceremony expected next month for 50 new houses for district staff.

The projects are aimed at improving office space and working conditions for district staff and supporting better service delivery.

item.title: Madang LLGs to benefit from amended liquor law
item.description: Local Level Government presidents in Madang Province have welcomed the recent amendments made to the Provincial Liquor Law by the Madang Provincial Assembly. The Provincial Liquor Control Bill was tabled by the chairman of law and order, Dum Bal, in the Provincial Assembly.
item.content:encoded:
Local Level Government presidents in Madang Province have welcomed the recent amendments made to the Provincial Liquor Law by the Madang Provincial Assembly.

The Provincial Liquor Control Bill was tabled by the chairman of law and order, Dum Bal, in the Provincial Assembly.

The amended law comes in nine parts and effectively repeals the 2009 Provincial Liquor Law.

The law basically allows the LLGs to generate some forms of revenue through registrations of liquor outlets within their respective LLG areas for the first time.

It also gives them allowance to pass their own LLG liquor by-laws and form their own LLG liquor boards to regulate the sale of alcohol.

President of Usino LLG, Charlie Wati, applauded chairman Bal for introducing the bill and the provincial assembly under the chairmanship of governor Ramsey Pariwa for voting unanimously to pass it.

"LLGs have been missing out on a lot of revenue in the past, and we are thankful the amended law now gives us the authority to collect some revenues, as well as create our own by- laws to regulate the sale of alcohol at the LLG level," Wati said.

"Previously, this power was with the Provincial Liquor Licensing Office only, and we missed out big time. We are happy that at least the new law is to our advantage.

"Alcohol alone has created a lot of social disorders in our communities, and hopefully, we can begin to see some improvements under the new Act."

Women and children's representative in the assembly, Margaret Anut, is equally excited that the new liquor law now empowers both the provincial and local level governments to impose tougher penalties on defaulters.

"There are a lot of grey areas in our provincial liquor act that needed tidying up, such as under-age drinking. Currently, children as young as 10 or 12 are buying and drinking alcohol and no one is doing anything. We need to also have proper monitoring mechanisms in place.

"The successful passage of this Bill will now create rooms for improvements," Ms. Anut said.

Meanwhile, a provincial liquor board is yet to be appointed to regulate this law.
